column1: # PlantCraft security check catalogue: the checks security-check.sh runs, as data. The bundle
# carries it under the signed SHA256SUMS; the script takes the severity, title and references
# from here, and PC-INT-01 checks this file and the script against the signed release.
# Columns (tab-separated): id, severity, title, references (IEC 62443-4-2 CR, NIST SP 800-53, CIS).

column3: The emergency administrator is kept for emergencies
Session cookies travel over HTTPS only
The API asks for sign-in
The data disk has room for the audit log and the series (more than 15% free)
The host clock is synchronised (NTP)
Every container runs as a user other than root
Every container has a read-only file system
Every container drops all capabilities and has no-new-privileges
Every container has a memory and a process limit
No container is privileged or shares the host's network or processes
Only the installer holds the Docker socket, and it has no network
Every container reports healthy
Docker Engine is a supported version (24 or later)
The Docker daemon has no open TCP socket and keeps containers up on restart
The host firewall is on
The data disk is encrypted
The host passes a Lynis audit (hardening index 70 or more, no warnings)
The host passes its OpenSCAP benchmark
The security check and its catalogue are the ones the signed release ships
The images in use are the ones the signed release lists
Installed apps are signed by a trusted publisher
Optional functions that are switched on
The public demo is off
No online catalog on an isolated install
The route lists (openapi.json) are not served
Only the proxy publishes a port on the host
The apps' networks have no way out (only edge, plant and egress reach outside)
The plant firewall rules are loaded (DOCKER-USER)
The last backup is less than a day old and verified
A restore was rehearsed in the last 90 days
Backups taken off the server are encrypted
Secret files are readable by their owner only
.env holds no secret and only its owner and group read it
The last backup holds the signing key and the session secret
The certificate is trusted (the plant's own, not the local CA)
The certificate is valid for more than 30 days
HTTPS answers carry HSTS and the security headers
Only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are accepted
Plain HTTP is redirected to HTTPS or closed
